## Overview

This appendix provides comprehensive documentation of all parameters and calculations used in the economic analysis of a 1% treaty and decentralized framework for drug assessment.

**Total parameters**: 351

- External sources (peer-reviewed): 138
- Calculated values: 116
- Core definitions: 97

### Quick Navigation

[Calculated Values](#sec-calculated) (116 parameters) • [External Data Sources](#sec-external) (138 parameters) • [Core Definitions](#sec-definitions) (97 parameters)


## Calculated Values {#sec-calculated}

Parameters derived from mathematical formulas and economic models.

### Additional Drug Approvals from Cost Elimination: 20 drugs/year {#sec-additional_drugs_from_cost_elimination}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Show full details"}

Additional drug approvals per year when Phase 2/3 cost barrier eliminated. Assumes valley-of-death compounds (abandoned due to cost) would have similar success rate to funded compounds.

**Inputs**:

- [Average Annual New Drug Approvals Globally](#sec-current_drug_approvals_per_year) 📊: 50 drugs/year (95% CI: 45 drugs/year - 60 drugs/year)
- [Valley of Death Attrition Rate](#sec-valley_of_death_attrition_pct) 📊: 40% (95% CI: 25% - 55%)

$$
AdditionalDrugs = 50 \text{ drugs/yr} \times 0.40 = 20 \text{ drugs/yr}
$$

*~ Medium confidence*

### Clinical Trial Cost Per Approved Drug: $1.20B {#sec-clinical_trial_cost_per_approved_drug}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Show full details"}

Annual clinical trial spending per approved drug (trials only, excluding other R&D costs like discovery, preclinical, manufacturing). Note: $60B ÷ 50 drugs = $1.2B per drug.

**Inputs**:

- [Annual Global Spending on Clinical Trials](#sec-global_clinical_trials_spending_annual) 📊: $60B (95% CI: $50B - $75B)
- [Average Annual New Drug Approvals Globally](#sec-current_drug_approvals_per_year) 📊: 50 drugs/year (95% CI: 45 drugs/year - 60 drugs/year)

$$
\text{Cost/Drug} = \frac{\$60B}{50} = \$1.2B
$$

*✓ High confidence*

### Combined Peace and Health Dividends for ROI Calculation: $144B {#sec-combined_peace_health_dividends_annual_for_roi_calc}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Show full details"}

Combined peace and health dividends for ROI calculation

**Inputs**:

- [Annual Peace Dividend from 1% Reduction in Total War Costs](#sec-peace_dividend_annual_societal_benefit) 🔢: $114B
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Annual Benefit: R&D Savings](#sec-dfda_benefit_rd_only_annual) 🔢: $30B

$$
Dividend_{ann} = Cost_{soc,ann} + Benefit_{DFDA,ann} = \$113.57B + \$30.00B = \$143.57B

### Total Annual Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Operational Costs: $40M {#sec-dfda_annual_opex}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Show full details"}

Total annual Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment operational costs (sum of all components: $15M + $10M + $8M + $5M + $2M)

**Inputs**:

- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Maintenance Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_platform_maintenance): $15M (95% CI: $10M - $22M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Staff Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_staff): $10M (95% CI: $7M - $15M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Infrastructure Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_infrastructure): $8M (95% CI: $5M - $12M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Regulatory Coordination Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_regulatory): $5M (95% CI: $3M - $8M)
- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Community Support Costs](#sec-dfda_opex_community): $2M (95% CI: $1M - $3M)

$$
OPEX_{total} = \$15M \text{ (plat)} + \$10M \text{ (staff)} + \$8M \text{ (infra)} + \$5M \text{ (reg)} + \$2M \text{ (comm)} = \$40M
$$

**Methodology**: [../appendix/dfda-cost-benefit-analysis#opex-breakdown](../appendix/dfda-cost-benefit-analysis#opex-breakdown)

### dFDA Combined Cure Speedup Multiplier: 13.3 multiplier {#sec-dfda_combined_cure_speedup_multiplier}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Show full details"}

Combined speedup factor for cure discovery from dFDA. Trial capacity multiplier (25.7×) times valley of death rescue (1.4×). With 36× speedup, diseases that would take T years to cure now take T/36 years.

**Inputs**:

- [Trial Capacity Multiplier](#sec-trial_capacity_multiplier) 🔢: 9.53 ratio
- [dFDA Valley of Death Rescue Multiplier](#sec-dfda_valley_of_death_rescue_multiplier) 🔢: 1.4 multiplier

$$
Speedup_{dFDA} = 25.7 \times 1.4 = 36\times
$$

*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

### Total Deaths from Disease Eradication Delay: 416M deaths {#sec-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_deaths_averted}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Show full details"}

Total eventually avoidable deaths from delaying disease eradication by 8.2 years (PRIMARY estimate, conservative). Excludes fundamentally unavoidable deaths (primarily accidents ~7.9%).

**Inputs**:

- [Regulatory Delay for Efficacy Testing Post-Safety Verification](#sec-efficacy_lag_years) 📊: 8.2 years (SE: ±2 years)
- [Global Daily Deaths from Disease and Aging](#sec-global_disease_deaths_daily) 📊: 150k deaths/day (SE: ±7.50k deaths/day)

$$
D_{total} = 54.75M \text{ (annual)} \times 8.2 \text{ (lag)} \times 92.1\% \text{ (avoidable)} = 413.4M
$$

**Methodology**: [../appendix/regulatory-mortality-analysis#disease-eradication-delay](../appendix/regulatory-mortality-analysis#disease-eradication-delay)

*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

{{< include ../figures/sensitivity-table-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_deaths_averted.qmd >}}

### Total Economic Loss from Disease Eradication Delay: $1.19 quadrillion {#sec-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_economic_value}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Show full details"}

Total economic loss from delaying disease eradication by 8.2 years (PRIMARY estimate, 2024 USD). Values global DALYs at standardized US/International normative rate ($150k) rather than local ability-to-pay, representing the full human capital loss.

**Inputs**:

- [Total DALYs Lost from Disease Eradication Delay](#sec-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_dalys) 🔢: 7.94B DALYs
- [Standard Economic Value per QALY](#sec-standard_economic_qaly_value_usd) 📊: $150K (SE: ±$30K)

$$
Loss = 7.90B \times \$150k = \$1.185\text{ quadrillion}
$$

**Methodology**: [../appendix/regulatory-mortality-analysis#economic-valuation](../appendix/regulatory-mortality-analysis#economic-valuation)

*~ Medium confidence*

### Years Lived with Disability During Disease Eradication Delay: 873M years {#sec-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_yld}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Show full details"}

Years Lived with Disability during disease eradication delay (PRIMARY estimate)

**Inputs**:

- [Total Deaths from Disease Eradication Delay](#sec-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_deaths_averted) 🔢: 416M deaths
- [Pre-Death Suffering Period During Post-Safety Efficacy Delay](#sec-regulatory_delay_suffering_period_years) 📊: 6 years (95% CI: 4 years - 9 years)

### Expected Treaty ROI (Risk-Adjusted): 300k {#sec-dfda_expected_roi}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Show full details"}

Expected ROI for 1% treaty accounting for political success probability uncertainty. Monte Carlo samples POLITICAL_SUCCESS_PROBABILITY from beta(0.1%, 10%) distribution to generate full expected value distribution. Central value uses 1% probability.

**Inputs**:

- [Treaty ROI - Full Timeline Shift (PRIMARY)](#sec-treaty_roi_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag) 🔢: 30.0M ratio
- [Political Success Probability](#sec-political_success_probability) 📊: 1% (95% CI: 0.1% - 10%)

$$
ROI_{DFDA,exp} = ROI_{treaty} \times Probability = 30M \times 1.0\% = 300{,}000
$$

**Methodology**: [Direct Calculation](#calculated)

*? Low confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

### NPV of Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Benefits (R&D Only, 10-Year Discounted): $199B {#sec-dfda_npv_benefit_rd_only}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Show full details"}

NPV of Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment R&D savings only with 5-year adoption ramp (10-year horizon, most conservative financial estimate)

**Inputs**:

- [Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment Annual Net Savings (R&D Only)](#sec-dfda_net_savings_rd_only_annual) 🔢: $30B
- [Standard Discount Rate for NPV Analysis](#sec-npv_discount_rate_standard): 3%

$$
PV_{benefits} = \sum_{t=1}^{10} \frac{NetSavings_{RD} \times \min(t,5)/5}{(1+r)^t} \approx \$249.3B \text{ (5-year linear adoption ramp)}
$$

**Methodology**: [../appendix/dfda-cost-benefit-analysis#npv-benefit](../appendix/dfda-cost-benefit-analysis#npv-benefit)

Years earlier the average cure arrives due to dFDA's trial capacity increase. With ~222 year baseline and ~23× speedup, cures arrive ~212 years earlier. Accel_{dFDA} = 222 \text{ yrs} \times (1 - \frac{1}{23}) = 212 \text{ years}

### Bed Nets Cost per DALY: $89 {#sec-bed_nets_cost_per_daly}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Show full details"}

GiveWell cost per DALY for insecticide-treated bed nets (midpoint estimate, range $78-100). DALYs (Disability-Adjusted Life Years) measure disease burden by combining years of life lost and years lived with disability. Bed nets prevent malaria deaths and are considered a gold standard benchmark for cost-effective global health interventions - if an intervention costs less per DALY than bed nets, it's exceptionally cost-effective. GiveWell synthesizes peer-reviewed academic research with transparent, rigorous methodology and extensive external expert review.

**Source**: [GiveWell - GiveWell Cost per Life Saved for Top Charities (2024)](../references.qmd#givewell-cost-per-life-saved)

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$78, $100] • Distribution: Normal

**What this means**: This estimate has moderate uncertainty. The true value likely falls between $78 and $100 (±12%). This represents a reasonable range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The normal distribution means values cluster around the center with equal chances of being higher or lower.*

#### Input Distribution

{{< include ../figures/distribution-bed_nets_cost_per_daly.qmd >}}

*✓ High confidence • 📊 Peer-reviewed*

:::

Percentage of deaths that are eventually avoidable with sufficient biomedical research and technological advancement. Central estimate ~92% based on ~7.9% fundamentally unavoidable (primarily accidents). Wide uncertainty reflects debate over: (1) aging as addressable vs. fundamental, (2) asymptotic difficulty of last diseases, (3) multifactorial disease complexity.

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [50%, 98%] • Distribution: Beta

**What this means**: There's significant uncertainty here. The true value likely falls between 50% and 98% (±26%). This represents a wide range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The beta distribution means values are bounded and can skew toward one end.*

*Core definition*

```{=html}
<script>
// Conservative lazy loading: only load images actually in viewport
(function() {
  'use strict';
  
  let imageObserver = null;
  let loadTimeout = null;
  
  function enableLazyLoading() {
    const images = document.querySelectorAll('img');
    
    // Use Intersection Observer with conservative threshold
    // rootMargin: '50px' means only load images within 50px of viewport
    // This prevents loading images passed through during hash navigation
    imageObserver = new IntersectionObserver((entries, observer) => {
      entries.forEach(entry => {
        if (entry.isIntersecting && entry.intersectionRatio > 0) {
          const img = entry.target;
          // Only load if image is actually visible (not just passed through)
          if (img.dataset.src) {
            img.src = img.dataset.src;
            img.removeAttribute('data-src');
          } else if (!img.hasAttribute('loading')) {
            // For images without data-src, use native lazy loading
            img.setAttribute('loading', 'lazy');
          }
          observer.unobserve(img);
        }
      });
    }, {
      rootMargin: '50px',  // Only load images within 50px of viewport
      threshold: 0.01      // Trigger when at least 1% visible
    });
    
    images.forEach(img => {
      imageObserver.observe(img);
    });
  }
  
  // Handle hash navigation (clicking links to sections)
  // Delay loading to avoid loading images passed through during jump
  function handleHashNavigation() {
    if (loadTimeout) clearTimeout(loadTimeout);
    // Wait 300ms after navigation to let scroll settle
    // Images will load naturally via Intersection Observer when visible
    loadTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
      // Scroll has settled, Intersection Observer will handle visible images
      // No action needed - observer is already watching
    }, 300);
  }
  
  // Initialize on page load
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', enableLazyLoading);
  } else {
    enableLazyLoading();
  }
  
  // Handle hash changes (clicking anchor links)
  window.addEventListener('hashchange', handleHashNavigation);
  
  // Also handle initial hash if page loads with one
  if (window.location.hash) {
    setTimeout(handleHashNavigation, 100);
  }
})();
</script>
```
